title: Circular Array Loop
summary: Given a circular array of non-zero integers, determine if a cycle exists by following movement rules based on the sign of each element.
statement: Given a circular array of non-zero integers, determine if a cycle exists by following movement rules based on the sign of each element. A cycle is identified if moving according to the rules results in a repeating sequence of indices, where all elements in the sequence are either positive or negative, and the sequence length is greater than one.
constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 5,000; -1,000 <= nums[i] <= 1,000 and every original entry is nonzero.
Move from i to (i+nums[i]) modulo n. A valid cycle uses at least two distinct indices and only one direction.
A same-index jump is invalid even if its magnitude exceeds n. Input mutation is allowed for the O(1)-extra-space follow-up.
hints: This is a directed graph with exactly one outgoing jump per index, plus direction and cycle-length rules.
Use slow/fast pointers on same-direction edges; reject self edges and stop at invalid or previously cleared entries.
After a failed search, walk its same-direction path again and mark those entries zero. Preserve the next index before clearing.
Cleared paths cannot contain a valid cycle. They are visited only a constant number of times, giving linear time and constant extra space.
editorial: Floyd pointers detect a repeated position without storing a visited set, but the next-step function must reject direction changes and self-jumps. After failure, clear the explored same-direction path using zero, which cannot occur in original inputs. Later searches stop at cleared nodes. The independent oracle follows every start, extracts the eventual cycle, and then checks its length and signs. Negative modulo results still designate valid circular indices.

tests.explanation: Indices 0→2→3→0 form a length-three cycle whose jumps are all positive.
The two positions repeat, but one jump is positive and one negative. This mixed-direction cycle is invalid.
